newsitem.title: USA: Va. gov seeks hike in education spending -- paper.
newsitem.headline: Va. gov seeks hike in education spending -- paper.

text.p: Virginia Gov. George Allen has proposed almost $30 million in new education spending, the Times-Dispatch reported Friday.

The plan would allocate $6.6 million to test first-graders for reading deficiences and provide remediation. Another $6.2 million would be spent on supplemental teaching materials. That would be in addition to the $64 million in current state funding for textbooks.

The new spending will be included when Allen formally proposes his changes to the state's two-year, $35 billion budget in an address to General Assembly finance committees next week, the newspaper said.
Last year, Allen urged the General Assembly to increase education spending by $1 billion, and about two-thirds of the increase was enacted.
